name: Floral amber fragrances

card.summary: A perfume subfamily pairing floral notes with warm amber (resins, sweet spices), chosen to give a scent that reads as rich and warm.

quick.overview:
Floral amber is a fragrance subfamily that blends flowers with warm amber accords such as resins and sweet spices. Wearers choose it to smell warm and distinctive, and it is one of the scent styles people use as part of overall presentation.

It is a perfumery classification rather than a studied appearance intervention. Fragrance categories come from industry tools such as the fragrance wheel.
quick.how: People pick a perfume or cologne in this family and apply it to pulse points or clothing, often for evenings or colder weather when heavier, warm scents are favored.
quick.risks: Fragrance can irritate skin or trigger allergies in some people. Strong scents may be unwelcome in shared spaces.

lead: Floral amber is a named subfamily of the floral group on the fragrance wheel, described as combining orange blossom and sweet spices [1]. The amber family, called oriental in older versions of the wheel, centers on resins and warm notes [1].

The wheel was created by perfume expert Michael Edwards in 1992 and revised through 2010, when the Oriental family was renamed Amber [1]. Its groupings are approximate and overlap between sources [1].

chain: Scent adds a distinct, warm impression
angle.text: Fragrance is part of how people present themselves; floral amber is chosen for a warm, rich impression.

paras: On Edwards' wheel, Floral includes Soft Floral and Floral Amber, while Amber includes Soft Amber and Woody Amber [1].

timeline.event: Michael Edwards creates the fragrance wheel [1].
Oriental family renamed Amber on the wheel [1].
